rounds.response:
Good questions — short answer: multiple regression is the same linear model extended to many predictors (written/solved compactly in matrix form), but it introduces important conceptual issues beyond "many simples," notably multicollinearity, larger/specialized variance and model‑selection concerns, and additional diagnostics (VIFs, partial residual/added‑variable plots, leverage/influence).  
Each coefficient βj is still the expected change in y for a one‑unit increase in Xj conditional on the other predictors (a partial effect), but when predictors are correlated that conditional contrast can be hypothetical or correspond to rare combinations and may make βj unstable or hard to interpret.  
For short answers, state the coefficient as a conditional/partial effect and then add a brief caveat if predictors are highly correlated (e.g., “holding other predictors fixed; note X and Z are correlated so this estimate may be imprecise/reflect extrapolation”).  
Always report diagnostic checks (correlations, VIFs, SEs/CIs, and a partial regression plot) and consider simplifying/regularizing the model if multicollinearity is a problem — tell me a specific coefficient and predictor pair if you want help wording the exact interpretation.
